newsitem.title: USA: Herbert Haft agrees to give up control of Dart-Post.
newsitem.headline: Herbert Haft agrees to give up control of Dart-Post.

text.p: Retail magnate Herbert Haft Monday agreed to accept a $42 million cash buyout to give up control of Dart Group Corp, the multimillion dollar retail empire he founded, the Washington Post reported Tuesday.

The tentative settlement between Haft and Dart was struck in the last moments before a Maryland bankruptcy judge was to have appointed a trustee to take control of the Haft family's real estate management company Combined Properties Inc.
The company had filed for bankruptcy protection from creditors in May 1995 as a result of a four-year-long open feud among family members for control of the companies.
If the settlement is accepted and other almost-settled Haft family issues are resolved, sources close to the deal said no Haft family member would be involved in running Dart.
The Dart Group includes Crown Books Corp., Trak Auto Corp. and Shoppers Food Warehouse Corp.
Lawyers for Dart and Haft said in court that a settlement of all other outstanding legal issues involving the Hafts is just days away.
"Hopefully it's going to all be over and done with soon," Ronald Haft told the newspaper. "You can see the whole family is involved and trying to get this thing wrapped up."
Dart is a retail holding company based in Landover, Md.
